title: Post office band and Navy Pier dance crowds
summary: Before joining Wickliffe he plays dances with the post office band and attends Navy Pier concerts, whose crowds include people escaping the summer heat.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: We came over. Before you joined Wycliffe, did you meet any fellas? Or get to know the jazz men around? Were you in any of the joints?

Oh, yes. I went to all the joints. And I was listening because I was very anxious to better, you know, better my playing. And the boys from the post office had a little band. And of course, in those days, I always had a violin. And so they asked me to come to rehearsal. To find out if I could play good enough. And I made the rehearsal. And they said it was fine. I played good and strong. You could hear me. And besides, I played in tune. I played pretty good. So I was enthused over it. So we rehearsed quite a long while. And then every time the post office clerks or somebody that they knew would give a dance, I started playing dances. And at the same time, whenever I got a chance, I always went down. Well, all during the summer, I went down to Navy Pier where Charles Elwood was playing so I could hear Darnell. And then...
What kind of crowds would they draw? A dance crowd?
A dance crowd, yes. It was a dance crowd. Well, of course, there was a lot of people that was escaping the heat from the city. They'd go and listen to. There was a lot of listeners.
